quote: Drift on the Stream of Infinite Flux, / Without joy, without fear: / When you must go—then go, / And make as little fuss as you can.
source: Tao Yuanming, Substance, Shadow, and Spirit, the close of Spirit expounds (trans. Arthur Waley, 1918)

evidence.where: the Constable 1918 first edition, read in the Cornell copy scanned by the Internet Archive and in the Project Gutenberg transcription of that edition; also compared with the Wikisource transcription of the 1919 Knopf printing
evidence.edition: A Hundred and Seventy Chinese Poems, translated by Arthur Waley (London: Constable and Company, 1918)
evidence.locator: Substance, Shadow, and Spirit (p. 73 onward), the section headed Spirit expounds, its last four lines, which close the poem. The Constable scan and Gutenberg both read Without joy, without fear; the 1919 Knopf transcription on Wikisource reads Without joy; without fear

reason: Read verbatim in the 1918 Constable text named by the proposal: the comma in line 2 is confirmed by the scan as well as by Gutenberg. The American printing differs by a semicolon, which is why the year and edition matter.
